question: How long does `verify --decode` of a TrueHD stream take when its scan and the decodes of its presentations run side by side, where each followed the one before?
method: `verify --decode` scanned a stream and then decoded every presentation it carries, one access unit in each presentation after another. The scan was put on a thread of its own, which tells the first major sync as soon as it has it; the decodes begin then, each presentation on a thread of its own, from the access units one more reader of the stream hands all of them, sixty-four at a time. The binary of main and the binary of the change were measured turn and turn about, five runs each (`tools/bench.py --compare`), on every command of the comparison, and on the longest stream there is with both bound to the fast cores. The effect is a factor of two to three, which two builds do not differ by, so it was not measured again inside one binary. That no report changed was looked for over the corpus (`tools/old_new.py --decode-all`, which runs `verify --decode` on every stream) and in the campaign of evidence 22. The streams are media and are not in the repository.

verify_decode_of_truehd.how: medians of five runs; the scan alone is `verify`, and the decode of a presentation is `decode -p N --format pcm`, whose own check of the stream runs on another thread
verify_decode_of_truehd.reading: the command takes what the decode of its widest presentation takes, where it took the scan and every presentation added up; the processor time is the same work on more threads, and the memory is two readers of the stream and the threads at once

the_longest_stream.how: `verify --decode` of a stream of 2.6 GB, the two binaries turn and turn about, two runs each after one that is not counted, bound to the fast cores

every_command_of_the_comparison.reading: none of the three runs the decodes of `verify --decode`. `verify` of an E-AC-3 stream runs nothing that changed; the two commands on TrueHD streams run the scan, which asks one question more for every unit, and the object format is written to a disk. Bound to the fast cores, eleven runs each and seven for the object format, they are within about one per cent of where they were

a_build_without_optimisation.what_happened: the first form handed the scan back from its thread by value. A scan is 49 248 bytes, and in a build without optimisation it stood on the stack of the thread that waited for it once for every function it passed through: `verify --decode` of the object fixture left with a stack overflow on Windows, where the main thread has a megabyte
a_build_without_optimisation.found_by: the test `verify_hands_back_the_report_the_command_prints_and_its_verdict`, which runs the command as a process; the tests that call the library run on threads with two megabytes and passed
a_build_without_optimisation.now: the scan goes onto the heap on the thread that made it, and only where it is goes back

each_new_one.mutation: the first major sync of a stream told again at every unit
the first major sync of a stream told to nobody
the decodes of verify --decode not begun when the scan has a major sync
the last units of a stream not handed to the decodes of its presentations
a decode of verify --decode handed every unit twice
the first unit of every hand-over not decoded
a presentation that stopped at a fault going on with the next unit
a presentation the stream carries left out of verify --decode

result.what_is_not_covered: One machine, with more processors than the command has threads: a stream of four presentations runs six. On fewer processors the command does the same work and gains less. That the threads run side by side is what the times show and no test asserts: a test holds every presentation to what its decode says by itself, on streams whole and damaged, which is true of one after another as well.

reading: `verify --decode` of a TrueHD stream takes 33.0 to 55.0 per cent of the time it took, on 10 streams of six to sixteen channels: it takes what the decode of its widest presentation takes (0.937 to 0.998 of it), where it took the scan and every presentation one after another. The processor time is 91.9 to 107.2 per cent of what it was and the memory 28.2 MiB at most where it was 18.8. The longest stream there is takes 46.7 s where it took 127.7. No report changes over the corpus.
